description: Through Field Shift, we help farmers in the Barind Tract chose better crop rotations by combining really environmental and soil data with their farming history, resources, and priorities.
summary: Orbit2Field (Field Shift) is a bilingual (English and Bangla) crop-rotation and zone-coordination web application built for smallholder farmers and agricultural extension officers in Bangladesh's drought-prone Barind tract (piloted across 52 unions in Godagari and Tanore, Rajshahi). For each farm, it combines live NASA POWER agro-climate records, cached NASA SMAP Level-4 root-zone soil moisture and MODIS NDVI vegetation data, and local SRDI/BARC soil profiles to score eight Barind crop rotations on water savings, soil health, profit, and climate risk. A System One decision model (Jev) picks an allowed rotation while scanning English and Bangla market headlines for early oversupply, a zone allocator balances crops across the upazila with seasonal fairness, and an open-weight language model explains the recommendation in plain language without altering any numbers.
details:
THE CHALLENGE IT ANSWERS In Bangladesh's High Barind tract, dry-season Boro rice relies heavily on pumped groundwater—a government water study reported the water table fell from ~8 m in the mid-1980s to ~18 m by 2021. Switching to lower-water winter crops helps, but when farmers switch without coordination, local markets crash: in 2025 Bangladesh produced roughly 2.5 million tonnes more potatoes than national demand, forcing growers to sell below cost. Farmers and extension officers need both plot-specific rotation guidance and upazila-level crop balance.

HOW ORBIT2FIELD WORKS

  1. Bilingual Field Intake (English & Bangla): Farmers or extension officers enter a farm name, pick an upazila and union across 52 pilot unions in Godagari and Tanore (Rajshahi), record their previous Rabi, Kharif-1, and Kharif-2 crops, water access (none, limited, reliable, plenty), budget tier, marketable crops, and priorities for water, soil, and profit.
  2. Live Climate, Satellite & Soil Pipeline: Server-side APIs query NASA POWER (2001–2020 climatology plus 2014–2024 monthly and daily temperature, precipitation, hot/cold days, and root-zone wetness) for the union's coordinates, enrich it with pre-fetched NASA AppEEARS SMAP Level-4 root-zone/surface soil moisture (SPL4SMGP.008) and MODIS 250 m NDVI vegetation time series (MOD13Q1.061), and merge union-level SRDI soil profiles (pH, organic matter, phosphorus, salinity/EC, texture, drainage) and BARC crop-suitability ratings.
  3. Rule-Based Scorer & System One (Jev) Selection: A deterministic scorer evaluates eight common Barind crop rotations across water fit, soil health (legume nitrogen credit, pH, drainage), relative profit margin, and heat risk, computing irrigation reductions versus Boro rice (for example, ~76% less irrigation for Lentil–Mungbean–T.Aman). TypeSafe AI's System One model (jev-1.13-free) selects one rotation from the allowed options with a confidence score and checks English and Bangla market headlines for early oversupply signals.
  4. Fair Upazila Zone Allocation (Neon Postgres): An upazila-level allocator stored in Neon Serverless Postgres enforces a per-crop rabi share cap (40% of farms normally, tightened to 25% when an early glut is detected). If a crop reaches its cap, the weakest-fit farm steps to its next-best viable rotation and receives priority status for the top crop next season.
  5. Grounded Natural-Language Explanations: Groq-hosted open-weight gpt-oss-120b (with gpt-oss-20b fallback and rule-based template fallback) translates the final assignment, soil direction, water impact, and risks into plain English and Bangla under strict JSON schema validation—without ever modifying scores or crop choices. Every source dataset and time series is inspectable on the app's /data transparency page.

WHAT WE WOULD BUILD NEXT

  • Replace placeholder crop margins and calendars with validated BARI/BRRI field-trial economics and sowing windows.
  • Automate scheduled AppEEARS satellite refreshes across all 52 unions and live Bangla/English agricultural price-feed ingestion.
  • Add SMS/IVR voice outreach for farmers without smartphones and cooperative/extension-officer dashboards for seasonal tracking.
